why: For each candidate hub [s,e], count the intervals that intersect it: all n minus those ending before s minus those starting after e. With starts and ends sorted, both counts are a binary search, so it is a sorting + binary search counting problem dressed as intervals.
hints: The statement already says it: pick a hub, keep everything touching it. The only question is how to count 'intervals touching [s,e]' fast for every hub.
Count the complement. An interval misses [s,e] only if it ends before s or starts after e, and these two cases never overlap. Sort all ends and all starts separately.
missed = bisect_left(ends, s) + (n - bisect_right(starts, e)); answer = min over hubs of missed. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Touching at an endpoint counts as intersecting: use strict comparisons (end < s, start > e) for 'missed'.
Duplicate intervals are allowed; binary search on sorted arrays handles them, a set would not.
An O(n^2) pairwise check times out at n = 10^5.
